title: Checking what you may legally do before you take a short-stay booking
audience: Property managers and hosts who arrange short-stay bookings for properties they manage or lease, or for owners.
learningOutcomes: Identify the kinds of approval a short-stay host may need to check, such as registration, permits, insurance and strata or body corporate rules.
Explain why the rules differ by state, territory and council, and why this lesson does not state them.
Describe the record to keep before a property is listed for short-stay bookings.

instruction.heading: Why this check comes first
instruction.body: A short-stay booking is a commercial use of a home, flat or room. Before a property is listed, the host or property manager must confirm that the use is allowed where the property is. This lesson sets out the questions to ask. It does not tell you the answers. Registration, permits, planning rules, levies, tax and insurance for short-stay letting differ between states, territories and local councils, and they change over time. Treat every answer in this lesson as UNCONFIRMED until the rule for the exact address has been checked against the current official source and recorded with its date.

instruction.heading: The questions to ask about each property
instruction.body: For each address, write down: whether the local council or state or territory authority requires a short-stay registration or permit, and whether it has a number that must be shown in listings; whether there are limits on nights per year or on the number of guests; whether the title, lease or body corporate or strata by-laws allow short-stay use at all; whether the owner's insurance covers short-stay guests, and whether the host's own cover does; and whether the tenancy or head-lease terms allow subletting or short-stay occupation. Each answer needs a source, a date checked and the name of the person who checked it. If any answer is not known, the property is not listed until it is.

instruction.heading: Authority you do not have
instruction.body: Completing this lesson does not give you a registration, a permit, an insurance policy or any right to let a property. Only the owner, the body corporate or strata manager, the landlord or head-lessor, the insurer and the relevant authority can give those. Where a lease or by-law prohibits short-stay use, the host must not list the property, even if a booking platform allows it. Where the owner has not given written instructions, do not accept bookings on their behalf.

instruction.heading: Record and review
instruction.body: Keep one record for each property with the checks made, the source link, the date checked, the person who checked, and the date the check must be repeated. Repeat the check when the lease renews, when the by-laws change, when the insurance renews, and when the council or the state or territory announces a change. A record that is more than a set period old must be treated as out of date until it is checked again. The review interval is a business standard to be set by the business owner and confirmed by the expert reviewer.

procedure: Collect the address, title or lease details, the body corporate or strata by-laws, and the owner's written instructions.
Check the local council and the state or territory requirements for short-stay registration, permits and any nights or guest limits, using the official source for that address.
Check the strata or body corporate by-laws and the lease or head-lease terms for any short-stay restriction.
Ask the owner's insurer in writing whether short-stay guests are covered, and keep the reply.
Record each answer with its source, the date checked and the checker's name.
Do not list the property until every answer is recorded and the owner has confirmed the listing in writing.
Set the date for the next check and add it to the property record.

workedExamples.situation: A two-bedroom flat in a strata building is offered for short-stay bookings by its owner. The owner says the council does not require registration.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you check before you accept the first booking?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner's statement is not a source. Check the council and the state or territory rules for the address, the strata by-laws for short-stay use, and the owner's insurance in writing. Record each source and the date. If the by-laws prohibit short-stay use, do not list the flat, even if the owner wants it listed. If the rules are confirmed to allow it, record the conditions, such as any nights limit, before listing.

workedExamples.situation: A property manager has three houses to list, and the insurance renewal for one of them falls due next week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How does the renewal change the plan?
workedExamples.reasoning: The short-stay insurance answer for that house is out of date at renewal. Ask the insurer in writing before the renewal whether short-stay guests are covered on the new terms. Do not take bookings for that house until the answer is recorded. The other two houses keep their own review dates.

equipmentAndPpe: The property record for each address, with the title or lease details and the by-laws.
A list of the official sources to check for the state or territory and council.
The owner's written instructions and the insurer's written reply.

commonErrors.error: Treating a booking platform's approval as proof that the property may be let short-stay.
commonErrors.prevention: A platform listing is not a permit or a by-law check. Record the rule and its source for the address.

commonErrors.error: Relying on a neighbour's or a previous host's registration for a different address.
commonErrors.prevention: Each address has its own rules and conditions. Check each property separately.

commonErrors.error: Assuming standard property insurance covers paying short-stay guests.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask the insurer in writing and keep the reply with the property record.

commonErrors.error: Recording a rule without its source or date.
commonErrors.prevention: A rule with no source and date is UNCONFIRMED. Do not act on it as fact.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Short-stay registration, permits, planning rules, nights limits and guest limits vary by state, territory and council. None of them is stated as fact in this lesson. UNCONFIRMED until checked for each address and date recorded. Flagged for expert review.

Strata and body corporate by-laws, leases and head-leases can prohibit short-stay use. Where they do, the property must not be listed. UNCONFIRMED in general terms; confirm for each property. Flagged for expert review.
Insurance for short-stay guests is a matter for the insurer's written terms. Nothing in this lesson describes any policy. UNCONFIRMED. Flagged for expert review.
This lesson does not grant registration, a permit, a tenancy right, a letting authority or an insurance cover. Completing it does not make anyone authorised to let a property.

qualityStandard: Every property listed for short-stay bookings has a record with each check answered, sourced and dated.
No property is listed while any answer is missing or the owner's written confirmation is absent.
Each check is repeated on its due date, and the due date is recorded.
documentationEvidence: Property record with the title or lease details, by-law check, council and state or territory check, and insurer reply.
Source link, date checked and checker name for each answer.
Owner's written instruction to list the property, and the next review date.
summary: Check whether short-stay use is allowed for each address before listing it.
Record each answer with its source, date and checker.
This lesson does not grant registration, a permit or insurance, and it does not state the rules for any place.

knowledgeChecks.question: A booking platform shows a property as available for short-stay bookings. What do you do?
options: List the property, because the platform has approved it
Check the rules for that address and the by-laws, and record the sources before listing
List it, and check later only if a guest complains

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is a recorded rule with no source or date treated as UNCONFIRMED?
options: Because the rule cannot be relied on for a decision until its source and date are known
Because the learner has to check it with the council first

knowledgeChecks.question: Which of these can finish a short-stay approval for a property?
options: The owner's written instruction together with the required registration and by-law checks
A neighbour's registration for another address
